topicName: Data Skew Handling and Shuffle Optimization
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Data Skew Handling and Shuffle Optimization in ETL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data skew is one of the most common bottlenecks in distributed ETL pipelines. It occurs when data is unevenly distributed across partitions, causing a few worker nodes to process the vast majority of the workload while others remain idle. This leads to severe performance degradation, memory errors, and increased job execution time."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Data Skew and Shuffles"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A shuffle is the process of redistributing data across different nodes, which typically happens during wide transformations like joins, aggregations (groupBy), and window functions. When a key is heavily skewed (e.g., NULL values or highly frequent domain keys), all records associated with that key are sent to a single partition and processed by a single task."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Technique 1: Salting for Skewed Joins"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Salting is a technique where you add a random prefix or suffix to the skewed join keys to distribute the data evenly across multiple partitions. Afterward, you expand the smaller dataframe to match the salted keys."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"import org.apache.spark.sql.functions._

val saltedDF = largeDF.withColumn("salt_key", concat(col("join_key"), lit("_"), floor(rand() * 10)))
val expandedSmallDF = smallDF.crossJoin(spark.range(10).toDF("id"))
  .withColumn("salt_key", concat(col("join_key"), lit("_"), col("id")))

val result = saltedDF.join(expandedSmallDF, "salt_key")"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Technique 2: Broadcast Hash Joins"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"If one of the datasets is relatively small, you can eliminate the shuffle entirely by broadcasting the small table to all executor nodes. This completely bypasses the shuffle phase and prevents data skew during joins."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import org.apache.spark.sql.functions.broadcast

val optimizedDF = largeDF.join(broadcast(smallDF), "id")"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Shuffle Optimization"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Increase shuffle partitions dynamically using spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to match your dataset size."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Filter out nulls or placeholder values before performing join operations if those keys are not required."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use AQE (Adaptive Query Execution) in modern Spark engines to automatically handle skew and coalesce partitions on the fly."}]
